sponsor_or_proposer: Marinvest Energy AS (Norway) / Marinvest Energy Canada
current_state: Norway's Marinvest Energy AS is in early talks with the federal government about a ~10 MTPA LNG export facility at Baie-Comeau, Quebec (floating offshore platforms + liquefaction plant + port infrastructure + a ~600-1000 km gas pipeline to TC Energy's Canadian Mainline, plus a possible dedicated wind farm for power). Ottawa has set up a multi-departmental 'deal team' to facilitate it and the IAAC has helped with First Nations engagement, but as of early 2026 Marinvest had NOT yet submitted a formal project description to the Major Projects Office or filed for environmental assessment. Comparable in scale to the cancelled GNL Quebec / Energie Saguenay.
missing_threshold_elements: Concrete step is borderline: federal facilitation and a deal team exist, but no project-description filing, EA registration, MOU/FEED contract, site lock, or land lease has been reported. Offshore platform siting not finalized. Location is at the project-area level (Baie-Comeau) but specific site/coordinates undisclosed.
watch_for: Submission of a project description to the federal Major Projects Office; IAAC/Quebec BAPE environmental-assessment registration; a named pipeline route; any MOU/FEED award or land/port lease; offtake agreements (re-check ~Q4 2026).
notes: NOT a duplicate of GEM's Energie Saguenay (GNL Quebec Inc, Port Saguenay, cancelled) — different sponsor, different location (Baie-Comeau vs Saguenay), distinct proposal. Entity Marinvest Energy AS not in GEM. National Observer coverage (nationalobserver.com 2026-02-20) corroborates but is 403-blocked to the verifier; CBC (cbc.ca/news/canada/montreal/quebec-lng-baie-comeau-1.7648993) and The Narwhal also cover it. Promote to new_terminal once a formal project description / EA filing appears.
